p.src: In the fourth month of summer, the seventh year of Jianxing of Shu-Han, Kongming's army was stationed at Mount Qi in three separate camps, awaiting the Wei forces.

u.src: In the fourth month of summer, the seventh year of Jianxing of Shu-Han, Kongming's army was stationed at Mount Qi in three separate camps, awaiting the Wei forces.

p.src: Meanwhile, Sima Yi led his army to Chang'an, where Zhang He received him and gave a full account of what had happened. Sima Yi appointed Zhang He as vanguard and Dai Ling as his deputy, and led a hundred thousand troops to Mount Qi, where they encamped south of the Wei River. Guo Huai and Sun Li entered the camp and paid their respects. Sima Yi asked, “Have you two yet faced the Shu army in battle?” The two replied, “We have not.” Sima Yi said, “The Shu army has come a thousand li, and its advantage lies in a swift battle; yet now that they are here, they do not fight. They must be plotting something. Has there been any news from the various routes through Longxi?” Guo Huai replied, “Our scouts have learned that every commandery is keeping the strictest watch day and night, and nothing untoward has occurred. Only Wudu and Yinping have yet to send reports.” Sima Yi said, “I shall send men of my own to engage Kongming. You two must hurry by the byroads to relieve those two commanderies, then come up behind the Shu army. Their ranks will surely fall into disorder.” The two accepted the plan and led five thousand troops along the byroads of Longxi to relieve Wudu and Yinping, intending then to strike the Shu army from the rear. On the way, Guo Huai said to Sun Li, “How does Zhongda compare with Kongming?” Sun Li replied, “Kongming is far superior to Zhongda.” Guo Huai said, “Though Kongming may be superior, this one plan alone shows that Zhongda possesses wisdom beyond ordinary men. If the Shu army is attacking the two commanderies in earnest and we sweep upon them from behind, how could they fail to fall into disorder?”

p.src: As they spoke, a scout suddenly rode up and reported, “Yinping has already fallen to Wang Ping, and Wudu has fallen to Jiang Wei. The Shu army is not far ahead.” Sun Li said, “If the Shu army has already taken the cities, why have they drawn up their forces outside them? There must be treachery here. We had best retreat at once.” Guo Huai agreed. Just as the order to retreat was being given, a cannon suddenly boomed, and a body of troops swept out from behind the mountain, bearing a banner emblazoned with the words “Zhuge Liang, Chancellor of Han”; at their center was a four-wheeled carriage, upon which Kongming sat upright; Guan Xing stood to his left and Zhang Bao to his right. Sun Li and Guo Huai were greatly alarmed at the sight. Kongming laughed loudly and cried, “Guo Huai and Sun Li, do not flee! How could Sima Yi's scheme deceive me? Each day he sends men to engage me at the front, while ordering you to strike the rear of my army. But I have already taken Wudu and Yinping. Why do you not surrender at once? Do you mean to drive your troops against me in a final contest?” When Guo Huai and Sun Li heard this, they were thrown into panic. Suddenly they were told that battle cries shook the heavens behind them: Wang Ping and Jiang Wei were leading troops in an attack from the rear. The two generals Guan Xing and Zhang Bao likewise led troops against them from the front. Attacked from both sides, the Wei army suffered a crushing defeat. Guo Huai and Sun Li abandoned their horses and fled up the mountain on foot. Zhang Bao caught sight of them and spurred his horse in pursuit; but unexpectedly, horse and rider tumbled together into a ravine. The rear guard hastened to rescue him, but his head had been split open in the fall, so Kongming had him sent back to Chengdu to recover.

p.src: Meanwhile, Guo Huai and Sun Li escaped and returned to Sima Yi, reporting, “The two commanderies of Wudu and Yinping have already been lost. Kongming lay in ambush at a strategic point and attacked us from front and rear. Thus we were soundly defeated and escaped only by abandoning our horses and fleeing on foot.” Sima Yi said, “The fault is not yours. Kongming's wisdom was one step ahead of mine. Lead troops once more to defend the two cities of Yong and Mei, and on no account give battle. I have a plan of my own for defeating the enemy.” The two bowed, took their leave, and departed. Sima Yi then summoned Zhang He and Dai Ling and instructed them, “Now that Kongming has taken Wudu and Yinping, he will surely be there soothing the people and settling their hearts, and will therefore be absent from his camp. Each of you is to lead ten thousand picked troops, set out tonight, circle behind the Shu army, and together charge upon them with all your might; I shall draw up my army at their front. As soon as the Shu ranks fall into confusion, I will drive my forces forward and storm their position. With our two armies joining strength, we can seize the Shu camp. Once we hold the mountainous ground there, how difficult could it be to defeat the enemy?”

p.src: The two accepted the plan and led their troops away. Dai Ling took the left. Zhang He took the right, each advancing by a byroad deep into the rear of the Shu army. At the third watch they reached the main road, where the two forces met and united, then advanced upon the Shu army from behind. Before they had gone thirty li, the vanguard halted. Zhang He and Dai Ling rode forward to see what was amiss and found several hundred carts laden with grass drawn crosswise across the road. Zhang He said, “They must have made preparations here. We must turn back at once.” No sooner had the order to retreat been given than fires blazed across the mountains, drums thundered mightily, and ambush troops poured out from every side, surrounding the two generals. From atop Mount Qi, Kongming called out, “Dai Ling and Zhang He, heed my words! Sima Yi reckoned that I would be in Wudu and Yinping soothing the people and absent from camp, and so he ordered you two to raid my encampment. Instead, you have fallen into my trap. You are but obscure junior officers. I will spare your lives—dismount and surrender at once!” Zhang He was enraged. Pointing at Kongming, he cursed, “You rustic recluse from the hills have invaded the borders of our great realm—how dare you utter such words! If ever I capture you, I shall hack your corpse into ten thousand pieces!” With that, he spurred his horse, leveled his spear, and charged up the mountain. Arrows and stones rained down from the heights. Unable to ascend the mountain, Zhang He wheeled his horse, brandished his spear, and burst through the encirclement, with none daring to stand against him. The Shu troops had Dai Ling trapped at the very center of the encirclement. After fighting his way out, Zhang He saw that Dai Ling was missing. Summoning his courage, he turned back and charged once more into the encirclement, rescued Dai Ling, and withdrew. From the mountain, Kongming watched Zhang He charge back and forth amid the host of soldiers. Seeing his valor redouble, he said to those around him, “I have often heard how Zhang Yide fought a great battle against Zhang He, striking fear into all who saw it. Only after seeing him today do I understand his courage. If this man is allowed to live, he will surely become a scourge to Shu. I must rid us of him.” He then withdrew his troops and returned to camp.

We had best withdraw for now.” He immediately ordered the whole army back to its main camp, which they were to defend without coming forth.

p.src: After hearing the edict, Kongming said to Fei Yi, “The affairs of our state are not yet accomplished. How can I resume the office of Chancellor?” He firmly declined to accept it. Fei Yi said, “If Your Excellency refuses the office, you will thwart the Emperor's wishes and dampen the spirits of the officers and soldiers. You should accept it for the time being.” Only then did Kongming bow and accept the appointment. Fei Yi took his leave and departed.

p.src: Seeing that Sima Yi would not come forth, Kongming devised a plan and ordered every camp to be struck and the army to move out. A spy duly reported to Sima Yi that Kongming had withdrawn his army. Yi said, “Kongming must have some great design. We must not move rashly.” Zhang He said, “He must be returning because his provisions are exhausted. Why should we not pursue him?” Yi said, “By my reckoning, Kongming gathered a great harvest last year, and now the wheat has ripened, so his provisions and fodder are abundant. Though transporting them is difficult, he can still hold out for half a year. Why would he leave so readily? He has seen that I have refused battle day after day, and so has contrived this ruse to lure me out. Send men to scout him from a great distance.” The soldiers reconnoitred and returned to report, “Kongming has encamped thirty li from here.” Yi said, “As I expected, Kongming has not truly gone. For now, hold the stockade firmly and do not advance rashly.” Ten days passed without the least word, and no Shu general appeared to offer battle. Yi again sent men to reconnoitre, and they returned to report, “The Shu army has broken camp and gone.” Yi did not believe them. Changing his clothes and mingling among the soldiers, he went to see for himself and found that the Shu army had indeed retreated another thirty li and made camp. Returning to camp, Yi told Zhang He, “This is one of Kongming’s schemes. We must not pursue.”

p.src: After another ten days, he again sent men to reconnoitre. They returned and reported, “The Shu army has retreated another thirty li and encamped.” Zhang He said, “Kongming is using a delaying stratagem to withdraw gradually to Hanzhong. Why does the Commander-in-Chief remain suspicious instead of pursuing him at once? I beg leave to go and decide the matter in battle!” Yi said, “Kongming has countless treacherous schemes. If anything goes amiss, the fighting spirit of our army will be broken. We must not advance rashly.” Zhang He said, “If I go and am defeated, I will gladly submit to military law.” Yi said, “Since you insist on going, we may divide the troops into two columns. You shall lead one column in advance and must fight with all your might, prepared to die. I shall follow in support and guard against ambush. Advance tomorrow and encamp halfway; then fight the day after, so that the soldiers will not lack strength.” The division of the troops was then completed. The next day, Zhang He and Dai Ling led several dozen deputy generals and thirty thousand picked troops boldly forward, then encamped halfway. Sima Yi left a large force of soldiers and cavalry to guard the camp and followed with only five thousand picked troops.

p.src: Kongming, meanwhile, had secretly sent scouts, who saw the Wei army halt midway. That night, Kongming summoned his generals and conferred with them, saying, “Now that the Wei army is coming in pursuit, they are certain to fight to the death. Each of you must be worth ten men. I shall use an ambush to cut off their rear, but none save a general of wisdom and courage can bear this charge.” As he finished, he looked toward Wei Yan. Wei Yan lowered his head and said nothing. Wang Ping stepped forward and said, “I am willing to undertake it.” Kongming said, “What if you fail?” Wang Ping replied, “I am willing to submit to military law.” Kongming sighed and said, “Wang Ping is willing to risk his life and brave the arrows and stones in person. He is truly a loyal minister! Even so, the Wei troops are coming in two columns, one behind the other, and will cut off my ambush in the middle. However wise and brave Wang Ping may be, he can oppose only one end; how can he divide himself between two places? It would be best to find another general to go with him. Alas, there is no one else in the army willing to risk death and take the lead!”

p.src: Before he had finished speaking, a general stepped forward and said, “I am willing to go!” Kongming looked and saw that it was Zhang Yi. Kongming said, “Zhang He is a renowned general of Wei, with courage enough to withstand ten thousand men. You are no match for him.” Zhang Yi said, “If anything goes amiss, I shall present my head beneath your tent.” Kongming said, “Since you dare to go, you and Wang Ping shall each lead ten thousand picked troops and lie in ambush in the mountain valleys. Wait until the Wei troops have caught up and let every one of them pass; then lead your hidden troops in an assault from the rear. If Sima Yi follows in pursuit, divide into two: Zhang Yi shall lead one force to hold off the rear column, while Wang Ping leads another to cut off the front. Both forces must fight to the death. I have another plan to aid you.” The two received their instructions and led their troops away.

p.src: Kongming then summoned Jiang Wei and Liao Hua and instructed them, “I give you two a brocade pouch. Lead three thousand picked troops, lower your banners, silence your drums, and lie in ambush upon the mountain ahead. If you see the Wei troops surround Wang Ping and Zhang Yi and the danger becomes extreme, do not go to their rescue. Simply open the pouch and read what is inside; there you will find a plan to relieve the danger.” The two received their instructions and led their troops away. He then called the four generals Wu Ban, Wu Yi, Ma Zhong, and Zhang Ni close and whispered his instructions: “If the Wei troops arrive tomorrow, their fighting spirit will be at its height. Do not meet them head-on, but fight as you withdraw. As soon as you see Guan Xing lead his troops in a flanking assault, turn your army and charge back. I shall have troops ready to support you.” The four generals received their instructions and led their troops away. He then summoned Guan Xing and instructed him, “Lead five thousand picked troops and lie in ambush in the mountain valley. When you see the red flag waving on the mountain, lead your troops out to attack.” Guan Xing received his instructions and led his troops away.

p.src: Now Zhang He and Dai Ling came on with their troops, swift as wind and rain. The four generals Ma Zhong, Zhang Ni, Wu Yi, and Wu Ban went out on horseback to meet them in combat. Zhang He flew into a rage and drove his troops after them. The Shu troops fought as they retreated. The Wei troops pursued them for more than twenty li. It was the sixth month and fiercely hot, and men and horses streamed with sweat as though drenched in water. By the time they had gone more than fifty li, all the Wei troops were gasping for breath. From the mountain, Kongming gave a signal with the red flag, and Guan Xing led his troops out to attack. Ma Zhong and the other three generals wheeled their troops about and charged back together. Zhang He and Dai Ling fought desperately and refused to retreat. Suddenly, tremendous battle cries arose as two forces charged out: they were Wang Ping and Zhang Yi. Both pressed the pursuit with great courage and cut off the enemy’s road of retreat. Zhang He cried out to his generals, “Now that you have come to this pass, if you do not fight to the death, what are you waiting for?” The Wei troops exerted all their strength to break through, but could not escape. Suddenly, drums and horns thundered behind them as Sima Yi himself arrived with his picked troops. Yi directed his generals and trapped Wang Ping and Zhang Yi in the heart of the encirclement. Zhang Yi cried aloud, “The Prime Minister is truly a man divine! He has already foreseen all this and must have an excellent plan. We must fight to the death!” They immediately divided their troops into two: Wang Ping led one force to hold Zhang He and Dai Ling at bay, while Zhang Yi led another to withstand Sima Yi with all its might. They fought desperately on both sides, and cries of battle filled the heavens. Jiang Wei and Liao Hua watched from the mountain. Seeing the Wei forces so powerful and the Shu troops in grave peril, gradually unable to hold out, Jiang Wei said to Liao Hua, “The danger is now so great that we may open the brocade pouch and see the plan.” The two opened it and read what was written inside: “If Sima Yi’s troops come and press Wang Ping and Zhang Yi hard in their encirclement, divide your forces into two columns and strike directly at Sima Yi’s camp. Yi will certainly retreat in haste, and you may attack amid the confusion. Even if you do not take the camp, you will win a complete victory.” The two were overjoyed. They immediately divided their troops into two columns and headed straight for Sima Yi’s camp.

u.src: Now Zhang He and Dai Ling came on with their troops, swift as wind and rain.
The four generals Ma Zhong, Zhang Ni, Wu Yi, and Wu Ban went out on horseback to meet them in combat.
Zhang He flew into a rage and drove his troops after them.
The Shu troops fought as they retreated.
The Wei troops pursued them for more than twenty li. It was the sixth month and fiercely hot, and men and horses streamed with sweat as though drenched in water.
By the time they had gone more than fifty li, all the Wei troops were gasping for breath.
From the mountain, Kongming gave a signal with the red flag, and Guan Xing led his troops out to attack.
Ma Zhong and the other three generals wheeled their troops about and charged back together.
Zhang He and Dai Ling fought desperately and refused to retreat.
Suddenly, tremendous battle cries arose as two forces charged out: they were Wang Ping and Zhang Yi.
Both pressed the pursuit with great courage and cut off the enemy’s road of retreat.
Zhang He cried out to his generals, “Now that you have come to this pass, if you do not fight to the death, what are you waiting for?”
The Wei troops exerted all their strength to break through, but could not escape.
Suddenly, drums and horns thundered behind them as Sima Yi himself arrived with his picked troops.
Yi directed his generals and trapped Wang Ping and Zhang Yi in the heart of the encirclement.
Zhang Yi cried aloud, “The Prime Minister is truly a man divine!
He has already foreseen all this and must have an excellent plan.
We must fight to the death!”
They immediately divided their troops into two: Wang Ping led one force to hold Zhang He and Dai Ling at bay, while Zhang Yi led another to withstand Sima Yi with all its might.
They fought desperately on both sides, and cries of battle filled the heavens.
Jiang Wei and Liao Hua watched from the mountain. Seeing the Wei forces so powerful and the Shu troops in grave peril, gradually unable to hold out,
Jiang Wei said to Liao Hua, “The danger is now so great that we may open the brocade pouch and see the plan.”

The two opened it and read what was written inside: “If Sima Yi’s troops come and press Wang Ping and Zhang Yi hard in their encirclement, divide your forces into two columns and strike directly at Sima Yi’s camp. Yi will certainly retreat in haste, and you may attack amid the confusion.
Even if you do not take the camp, you will win a complete victory.”
The two were overjoyed. They immediately divided their troops into two columns and headed straight for Sima Yi’s camp.

p.src: Sima Yi, fearing that he might fall into Kongming’s trap, had also kept men relaying reports to him all along the way. Just as Sima Yi was urging his men on in battle, a swift courier suddenly galloped up to report that the Shu forces were advancing by two routes straight toward the main camp. Sima Yi turned pale with alarm and said to his generals, “I knew Kongming had a stratagem, but none of you believed me. You forced me to pursue him, and now you have ruined our great undertaking!” He immediately turned his army about and hurried back. Panic swept through the ranks, and the soldiers fled in disorder. Zhang Yi pursued and struck them from behind, inflicting a crushing defeat on the Wei army. Seeing themselves isolated, Zhang He and Dai Ling also fled along a secluded mountain path, and the Shu army won a great victory. Guan Xing came up behind with troops to support the various columns. After suffering this severe defeat, Sima Yi fled back into his camp, but by then the Shu forces had already withdrawn. Sima Yi gathered the routed troops and rebuked his generals: “You know nothing of the art of war and rely only on hot-blooded courage. By insisting upon battle, you have brought about this defeat. Henceforth, you are strictly forbidden to act rashly. Whoever disobeys again will assuredly be punished under military law!” All withdrew in shame. In this battle, vast numbers of Wei soldiers were killed, and countless horses, weapons, and other equipment were abandoned.

p.src: Ten days later, Kongming summoned Dong Jue, Fan Jian, and the others to his tent and instructed them: “I feel myself growing faint and muddled and can no longer attend to affairs. It would be better to return to Hanzhong for a time and recuperate, then devise a sound plan anew. You must take great care not to let word escape. If Sima Yi learns of it, he will certainly attack.” He then issued orders for the camp to be secretly struck that night and for the entire army to return to Hanzhong. Only five days after Kongming had departed did Sima Yi learn of it. He sighed deeply and said, “Kongming’s stratagems truly appear and vanish like spirits and demons. I cannot equal him!” Sima Yi then left the generals in the camp and divided the troops among the various strategic passes to guard them; he himself withdrew with the main army.

p.src: Meanwhile, Kongming stationed the main army at Hanzhong and returned alone to Chengdu to recuperate. The civil and military officials came out of the city to meet him and escorted him to the Chancellor’s residence. The Latter Emperor came in person to inquire after his health and ordered the imperial physicians to treat him, so that he gradually recovered.

p.src: In the seventh month of autumn in the eighth year of Jianxing, the Wei commander Cao Zhen recovered from his illness and submitted a memorial: “The forces of Shu have repeatedly invaded our borders and made incursions into the Central Plain. Unless they are destroyed, they will surely become a future menace. Now the cool autumn season has arrived, and men and horses are rested; this is precisely the time to launch a campaign. I ask leave to lead the great army together with Sima Yi, march straight into Hanzhong, annihilate the rebel faction, and secure the frontier.” The ruler of Wei was delighted and asked Palace Attendant Liu Ye, “Zidan urges me to attack Shu. What do you think?” Liu Ye replied, “The General-in-Chief speaks rightly. If we do not destroy them now, they will surely become a grave menace hereafter. Your Majesty should proceed with the campaign at once.” Cao Rui nodded. After Liu Ye left the palace and returned home, a number of high ministers came to visit and asked, “We hear that His Majesty discussed with you the raising of an army against Shu. What do you think of the matter?” Liu Ye answered, “There is no such matter. Shu is protected by perilous mountains and rivers and cannot easily be taken. To exhaust soldiers and horses to no purpose would bring the state no benefit.” The officials withdrew in silence. Yang Ji entered the palace and reported: “Yesterday I heard that Liu Ye urged Your Majesty to attack Shu, yet today, when discussing the matter with the ministers, he said Shu should not be attacked. He is deceiving Your Majesty. Why does Your Majesty not summon and question him?” Cao Rui immediately summoned Liu Ye and asked him, “You urged me to attack Shu, but now you say it cannot be attacked. Why is that?” Liu Ye said, “Upon considering the matter closely, I find that Shu cannot be attacked.” Cao Rui laughed heartily. A short while later, Yang Ji left the palace. Liu Ye then reported, “Yesterday I urged Your Majesty to attack Shu. This is a great matter of state; how could it carelessly be divulged to others? Warfare is the way of deception. Before the undertaking begins, it must be kept strictly secret.” Cao Rui understood at once and said, “You are right.” From that time on, he held Liu Ye in still greater esteem.

p.src: Within ten days, Sima Yi appeared at court, and the ruler of Wei related to him, point by point, the contents of Cao Zhen’s memorial. Sima Yi replied, “In my judgment, Eastern Wu will certainly not dare to move its forces. Now is precisely the time to take advantage of this and attack Shu.” Cao Rui immediately appointed Cao Zhen Grand Marshal and Commander-in-Chief of the Western Expedition, Sima Yi General-in-Chief and Deputy Commander of the Western Expedition, and Liu Ye military adviser. The three took leave of the ruler of Wei and led an army of four hundred thousand first to Chang’an, then marched straight toward Jiange to seize Hanzhong. The remaining commanders, including Guo Huai and Sun Li, each advanced by a separate route.

p.src: Men from Hanzhong carried the news to Chengdu. By this time Kongming had long since recovered. Each day he drilled his troops and trained them in the Eight Formations until all had mastered them, for he intended to seize the Central Plain. On hearing the news, he summoned Zhang Yi and Wang Ping and instructed them: “You two are to take one thousand men in advance and guard the old Chencang road against the Wei forces. I shall lead the main army after you in support.” The two protested, “Reports say the Wei army numbers four hundred thousand, though it falsely claims eight hundred thousand, and its might is tremendous. How can we be sent with only one thousand men to guard the pass? If the Wei forces arrive in full strength, how are we to resist them?” Kongming replied, “I would give you more men, but I fear only that the soldiers would suffer needless hardship.” Zhang Yi and Wang Ping looked at each other, and neither dared to depart. Kongming said, “If anything should go amiss, the fault will not be yours. Say no more. Make haste and go.” The two pleaded again, “If the Chancellor wishes to put the two of us to death, then we beg to be executed here and now. We simply dare not go.” Kongming laughed and said, “How foolish you are! I have my own reasons for sending you. Last night I looked up and studied the heavens. I saw the Pi star entering the lunar region of Taiyin; within this month there will surely be torrential rain. Though the Wei army numbers four hundred thousand, how would it dare advance deep into such perilous mountains? That is why you need no large force; you will certainly come to no harm. I shall keep the main army resting in Hanzhong for a full month. When the Wei army withdraws, I shall swiftly sally forth with the main force and fall upon it. By meeting the weary with the rested, my hundred thousand men can defeat Wei’s four hundred thousand.” Only after hearing this were the two overjoyed. They bowed farewell and departed. Kongming then led the main army out of Hanzhong. He issued orders that every strategic pass prepare dry firewood, fodder, and fine grain, enough to sustain men and horses for one month against the autumn rains. He granted the main army a month’s respite, issued clothing and provisions in advance, and had the troops await the order to campaign.

If we penetrate deep into hostile territory, all will be well should we win; but if some mishap occurs, men and horses will suffer, and retreat will be difficult. For now, we should erect huts within the city and encamp here against the coming rains.” Cao Zhen followed his advice.
